content: Note that I will focus on the key points of each interaction while maintaining the detailed nature of the information. 1. Avoid or use an alternative drug when co-administering glecaprevir/pibrentasvir with darunavir, as darunavir is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor and P-glycoprotein (P-gp) substrate, which can significantly alter drug levels. 2. Monitor closely when glecaprevir/pibrentasvir is co-administered with dasabuvir, as it increases dasabuvir levels by inhibiting P-gp efflux transporters. Adjust therapy as needed. 3. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases daunorubicin levels by inhibiting P-gp efflux transporters and reducing metabolism. Use caution and monitor for toxicity. 4. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase plasma concentrations of drugs that are substrates of breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP). Monitor closely for potential adverse effects. 5. Co-administration of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir with desloratadine increases desloratadine levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor for side effects. 6. Dexamethasone decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for reduced therapeutic efficacy. 7. Drugs that induce CYP3A4, when co-administered with glecaprevir/pibrentasvir, may decrease its plasma concentrations, potentially reducing its therapeutic effect. Monitor closely. 8. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases digoxin levels by inhibiting P-gp efflux transporters. Measure serum digoxin concentrations before initiating therapy and adjust the dose by approximately 50% if necessary. 9. Co-administration with diltiazem increases diltiazem levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor for potential toxicity. 10. Dipyridamole increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by inhibiting P-gp and reducing metabolism. Conversely, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases dipyridamole levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases docetaxel levels via P-gp inhibition. Monitor closely for signs of toxicity. 12. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases doxorubicin levels by inhibiting P-gp and reducing metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 13. Dronedarone increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Drospirenone increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 15. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases duvelisib levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor for toxicity. 16. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases edoxaban levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Efavirenz decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug to prevent loss of therapeutic effect. 18. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases elagolix levels via P-gp inhibition, while elagolix decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or modify therapy as needed. 19. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases elbasvir/grazoprevir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Co-administration with eletriptan increases eletriptan levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 21. Eliglustat increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Eltrombopag increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 23. Eluxadoline increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels, while glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may reduce eluxadoline’s therapeutic effects. Monitor closely for toxicity and efficacy. 24. Grapefruit increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases hydrocortisone levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor for side effects. 26. Ibrutinib increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases idarubicin levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor for toxicity. 28. Idelalisib increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Imatinib increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases imatinib levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Indinavir increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases indinavir levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases irinotecan levels via P-gp inhibition. Monitor closely for signs of toxicity.
